main_text.p: tempus, vt gentes abstinerent à sanguine & suffocato, idque nullam aliam ob causam, nisi propter charitatem: nil statuit cōtra Christum, sed cum Christo.
Secundus locus est Act. 2. 8. 10. 19. Baptizarunt in nomine Christi, contra mandatum Christi, Matth. 28.

Respondent Primò Patres: etsi baptizarunt in nomine Christi: non sequitur, eos non baptizasse in nomen Patris & Spiritus sancti. Prima ratio: cùm ij tres unum sint: Secunda ratio: Et in nomine Christi, quod significat vnctum, necessariò intelligantur Pater, qui vnxit: Filius, qui vnctus est: & Spiritus sanctus, quo vnctus est. Tertia ratio: Et Christus ait, Qui credit in me, non credit in me (scilicet solum) sed in eum qui misit me. Ergo etiam qui baptizabatur in nomine Christi, non in eum solum, sed etiam in Patrem baptizabatur. Quare quoad substantiam, nihil mutarunt in forma baptismi praescripta à Christo. Et haec responsio Patrum non potest nec debet reiici à Papistis. Sic esset fallacia diuisionis.

Secundò: Noftri: Ex his locis non potest concludi, Apostolos non vsurpasse formam à Christo praescriptam. Ratio est: quia cùm ita loquitur Lucas, & iussi sunt baptizari in nomine Christi. Item, & baptizati sunt in nomine Christi: non significat, Apostolos iis verbis vsos fuisse: Ego te baptizo in nomine Christi. Sed quid voluit significare? Quidam: voluit

page.notes: Greek ampersand-like signs (&) are printed as the Latin "&" abbreviation of et. Several italic words and the Greek-looking "&" symbols are as printed. Printed text is faint at the right edge and the final line is partly cut off by the gutter; the last word "voluit" continues in the catchword position at the bottom right, shown as "luit" on the scan. Some words in the main line are doubtful: "vnctum" and "fubstantiam" were read from the scan with uncertainty; "Papiftis" likely as printed. The stroke "[?]" was not required because the reading is clear.
